candidates.name: Yelp/dataset-examples
candidates.what_it_holds: Archived (read-only since May 2025) official Yelp repo with example scripts (JSON-to-CSV converter, category predictor, review generator, word-positivity scorer) for the Yelp Academic/Open Dataset, which itself is hosted at yelp.com/dataset (businesses, reviews, users, checkins, tips across multiple US/Canada metros, updated periodically by Yelp, JSON format, several GB). 45 commits, Python 2.6+/mrjob based.
candidates.why_useful: Yelp business density/review-volume/rating trends by metro are a leisure/dining-demand proxy correlated with local tourism and short-term-rental attractiveness (gap #6, restaurant-adjacent leisure proxy); the actual dataset must be pulled from yelp.com, not GitHub, hence pointer_to_external_host.
candidates.license: custom Yelp dataset terms (non-commercial, academic use) for the data; repo code license unspecified
candidates.last_activity: archived 2025-05-13; underlying dataset periodically refreshed by Yelp
candidates.time_coverage: multi-year, vintage depends on current Yelp dataset release

candidates.name: gosom/google-maps-scraper
candidates.what_it_holds: Go/Playwright based scraper extracting 36+ fields per Google Maps business listing (name, address, GPS, rating, review count, reviews with timestamps/ratings, hours, price range, categories). CLI/Web UI/REST API/self-hosted SaaS modes, Docker/Kubernetes support. MIT license, ~5,800 stars, 333 commits, actively maintained.
candidates.why_useful: A working, well-maintained method to pull rating/review-volume time series for restaurants and leisure venues by city as a local leisure/tourism-activity proxy, and potentially for competitor STR listings' Google Maps presence; usable within the fee-panel style sanctioned scraping decision (a human call per rules).

candidates.name: omkarcloud/google-maps-scraper
candidates.what_it_holds: Python Google Maps business scraper, 50+ fields (name, address, phone, website, emails, socials, ratings, reviews), CLI + Python/Node API, free tier 200 searches/month. MIT license, ~3.5k stars, 209 commits.
candidates.why_useful: Alternative/competing Google Maps scraping method to gosom's for leisure/restaurant/venue density and rating trends by market; same leisure-proxy rationale.

candidates.name: omkarcloud/google-maps-reviews-scraper
candidates.what_it_holds: Dedicated Google Maps reviews-only scraper (182 stars) for extracting review text/ratings/dates from a place, separate from the general business-listing scraper by the same author.
candidates.why_useful: Could build a review-volume-over-time series (a nowcast proxy for foot traffic/leisure activity at specific venues or markets) similar to the team's existing Inside Airbnb reviews-based stays index methodology.

candidates.name: omkarcloud/tripadvisor-scraper
candidates.what_it_holds: TripAdvisor scraper (212 stars) extracting hotel/restaurant names, ratings, reviews, and contact info.
candidates.why_useful: TripAdvisor review volume/ratings for hotels and restaurants by market is another leisure/travel-demand proxy, and could give a competitor/adjacent-lodging read (hotel review volume as an occupancy proxy) alongside the existing hotel RevPAR data.

candidates.name: RUCAIBox/RecSysDatasets
candidates.what_it_holds: Curated download/preprocess toolkit (302 commits) converting many public recommender-system datasets into a unified 'atomic file' format for the RecBole library, including Foursquare (NYC and Tokyo check-ins) and Gowalla (global check-in dataset), plus 5 versions of the Yelp dataset (2018-2022), Amazon reviews (1996-2023), Tmall, and others.
candidates.why_useful: Fills gap #20 (party size / group travel / geotagged tourism datasets): Foursquare NYC/Tokyo and Gowalla give geotagged check-in mobility panels that are a free proxy for leisure travel/visitation patterns in specific cities, and the repo is a one-command way to pull and normalize them (rather than chasing the original academic hosts by hand).
candidates.license: unspecified on repo page (datasets carry their own academic-use terms)
candidates.geography: Foursquare: NYC, Tokyo; Gowalla: global; Yelp: US/Canada metros
candidates.time_coverage: Foursquare/Gowalla check-ins ~2009-2013 (historical, academic datasets); Yelp 2018-2022 dataset snapshots
candidates.size_hint: Foursquare NYC/Tokyo check-in sets are ~100k-500k rows each; Gowalla ~6.4M checkins over 196k users (as originally published)

candidates.name: issacchan26/OpenTableReviewsScraping
candidates.what_it_holds: Small web-scraping script to collect OpenTable restaurant reviews (last commit Oct 2023). No committed dataset visible, no clear geography stated, low star/maintenance signal.
candidates.why_useful: Only OpenTable-adjacent GitHub repo found under the 'opentable' topic; does not touch OpenTable's actual 'State of the Industry' seated-diners index (that specific dataset/API does not appear to have any GitHub mirror, scraper, or topic — searched directly, topic pages for opentable-scraper and opentable-state-of-industry are both unused). Low confidence this repo is still functional or maintained.

candidates.name: ticketpy (Ticketmaster Discovery API Python wrapper)
candidates.what_it_holds: Python SDK/wrapper (29 stars) for the Ticketmaster Discovery API, which exposes event listings (concerts, sports, festivals) with venue, date, and location metadata across the US and internationally where Ticketmaster operates.
candidates.why_useful: A ready client for pulling event density by city/date as an events/shocks proxy (gap #11: FIFA World Cup 2026, concerts, conferences) that could feed a city-level event calendar to explain short-term nights/ADR spikes; requires a free Ticketmaster Discovery API key, no scraping of a login-walled site.
candidates.last_activity: unspecified, low star count suggests light maintenance
candidates.time_coverage: forward-looking event calendar, not historical panel

candidates.name: actor-ticketmaster-scraper (Apify actor)
candidates.what_it_holds: Apify-hosted scraper (16 stars) for Ticketmaster event listings by category, an alternative to the official API wrapper for pulling event/venue/date data.
candidates.why_useful: Same events-calendar use case as ticketpy above (gap #11) if the official API's coverage or rate limits are insufficient; runs on Apify's platform rather than being a self-contained repo.

notes: Hit a hard wall this pass: this session's WebSearch tool returned 'budget exhausted (200/200)' on the very first three queries (shared session-wide across scouts, not per-theme), and github.com/search (both UI search and code search) returned HTTP 429 rate-limited for the rest of the run, refreshing only after ~1 hour per the Retry-After header. All findings above came from direct WebFetch of github.com/<owner>/<repo> pages and github.com/topics/<tag> pages, which were NOT rate-limited — this is a workable fallback for future scouts if WebSearch/search API are both blocked. Specific dead end: OpenTable's actual 'State of the Industry' seated-diners YoY dataset (the thing named in this theme) does not appear to have any GitHub presence at all — no repo, no topic tag, no scraper — under the topics opentable, opentable-scraper, opentable-state-of-industry, opentable-api, dining, or restaurant-data; a future scout with a working search API should try Google-indexed blog posts/journalist writeups (Axios, The Economist, NYT used this data during COVID) that might link to a scraper or CSV mirror I couldn't reach here. The 'restaurant-data', 'dining', 'ticketmaster', 'eventbrite', 'songkick', and 'setlist-fm' GitHub topics are dominated by personal-project API wrappers, Spotify-playlist mashups, and ML-boilerplate notebooks on the single well-known datasets — excluded per instructions. The most substantive real finds are the Yelp official dataset pointer, two Google Maps scraper families (gosom's is the most actively maintained), a TripAdvisor scraper, and RUCAIBox/RecSysDatasets which is a genuinely useful one-command downloader for Foursquare NYC/Tokyo and Gowalla check-in mobility panels (fills gap #20) plus multiple Yelp dataset vintages. Suggest a future scout with search access specifically target: (a) 'opentable' + 'axios' or 'economist' data journalism repos, (b) Eventbrite/Bandsintown aggregate event-count APIs rather than personal wrappers, (c) Zomato/Swiggy India restaurant datasets only if a China/India geography gap opens up (currently out of scope for ABNB's core markets in CONTEXT.md).
